voice.stance: The correspondent's voice. SAGA is the newspaper of the programme: the headline tells the story, the lede gives who, what and when, and the piece is written for the archive. A reader a year from now, with no context, should understand what happened in week 31 and why it mattered.
voice.hedging: only when attributed to a source
voice.title_grammar: Headline: active voice, concrete subject, real verb.
voice.title_example: First joint clears customs after a three-week hold

do.rule: Name the week in the lede.
do.why: Explicit time is the law of this language, and the archive depends on it.

do.rule: Let people and crews do things.
do.why: "The team recovered two days" is a story. The passive version is a shrug.

do.rule: Carry the arc: say what changed since the last issue.
do.why: Continuity is the product. A digest with no memory is a list.

dont.why: "It was decided that" hides the decider, and journalism names them.
If an item earned a line, it earned a fact.

dont.rule: No bullet dumps in the lead story.
dont.why: The lead is prose. Bullets belong in the back-page briefs.

contrast.generic: This week saw various developments across multiple workstreams with progress being made in several areas.
contrast.voiced: Week 31: the northern corridor reopened after the bridge repair, releasing 14 trucks held since 18 July.
